hero-description: Creation of the online store for Elise, creator of upcycled art objects
hero-add: In collaboration with Clara and Elise
s1-sub: Elise creates upcycled handmade objects: she finds pieces at flea markets and transforms them.
s1-p1: In summer 2025, she posted her creations on Instagram with a reel per creation for a few days. Her account exploded: it went from 100 to 7,000 followers.
s1-p2: People interested in her creations were writing to her to buy, but she had no way to sell.
s1-p3: This need became our M2 web project: create an e-commerce site for Elise, with an almost zero budget, in one semester. Elise was the client and a team member. Clara was project manager and designer.
s1-p4: → I was in charge of user research.
s1-p5: I also handled the site's development on WordPress and helped shape the art direction.
s2-p1: We structured the project around a design sprint week to quickly frame the problem and align the team on the value proposition, needs, targets, and constraints.
s2-p2: During this framing we created a benchmark, a BMC, and 3 user journeys (CJM customer journey maps) linked to 3 personas: someone from Elise's circle, Elise's Instagram follower, and the potential partner.
s2-p3: For a first version of the site, we focused on the first two personas, the third being less vital to the primary need of online selling.
s3-p1: Following this week, I was able to design the user testing protocol by writing the interview guide.
s3-p2: I then ran in-person sessions with 7 participants: 3 respondents from Élise's circle, 3 Instagram follower respondents and 1 respondent with an external profile. Finally, I transcribed and analyzed the interviews.
s4-p1: Working on this project was a real source of motivation because it was a concrete case, guided by real needs.
s4-p2: I found it very interesting to discover the ecosystem of craftsmanship, upcycling and independent creators, as well as the thought mechanics that motivate (or not) a user to buy.
s4-p3: Moreover, this experience confirmed my interest in user research 💫
